graph.title: Arrays (Arduino built-in example): six LEDs on pins 2-7
notes: The breadboard in the picture is drawn flipped relative to the catalogue naming: the image's top half (rows j-f) is mapped to bank 'b' (rows f-j) and the bottom half (rows e-a) to bank 't' (rows a-e). Resistors straddle the centre gap.
Column numbers are read from the image: LED anodes/resistors/signal wires in columns 7, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22 (pins 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 respectively); LED cathodes in columns 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23.

Each LED cathode connects with a short black jumper to the top ground rail (tn); the exact rail hole index is approximate, all rail holes are one strip. One black jumper runs from Arduino GND (next to pin 13) to the same rail.
The manual text says 220 ohm resistors; the catalogue resistor is generic so value=220 is set as a prop.
The schematic shows pin order 7,6,5,4,3,2 top to bottom; the sketch's array order (2,7,4,6,5,3) only affects software, not wiring.
Manual lists 'hook-up wires' as one item; 14 jumper wires are used in the circuit image: 6 signal, 6 LED ground, 1 Arduino GND (13 total counting these: 6+6+1).

breadboard.name: Solderless breadboard
breadboard.port_rule: Holes are named '<column><bank>.<row>': column 1-30, bank 't' (top half, rows a-e) or 'b' (bottom half, rows f-j), e.g. '12t.c', '7b.h'. The 5 holes of one column-bank are one strip. Power rails: 'tp.<n>', 'tn.<n>', 'bp.<n>', 'bn.<n>' (each rail is one strip).
